title: Yao's Conjecture (Quantum Sorting Lower Bound)
statement_text: The quantum query complexity of sorting under partial information, given any poset $P$ on $n$ elements, is at least $c \log(|\Delta(P)|)$ for some universal constant $c > 0$.
context_text: Yao (STOC'04) proved a weaker lower bound of $c\log(|\Delta(P)|) - c'n$ for universal constants $c, c' > 0$, which is useless when the information-theoretic lower bound is $o(n)$. He conjectured that the linear correction term is unnecessary and the information-theoretic lower bound holds for any partial order $P$ up to a constant factor. Section 4 of the paper is titled 'A proof of Yao's conjecture for series-parallel posets'.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for the class of series-parallel posets (Theorem 2) and extends it to the wider class of extended series-parallel posets, which includes posets with $\Omega(n^4)$ induced $N$-subposets (Corollary 1).
paper_title: Information-theoretic lower bounds for quantum sorting

title: Conjecture on LB and QLB equivalence
statement_text: The two lower bounds $\mathrm{LB}(P)$ and $\mathrm{QLB}(P)$ are within a constant factor of each other for all posets $P$.
context_text: Let $P=([n],\le_P)$ be a poset and $\Delta(P)$ its set of linear extensions. Sorting under partial information means determining the unknown linear extension by comparisons; the information-theoretic lower bound is $\ln|\Delta(P)|$ (natural logarithms). The chain polytope $C(P)$ is the set of $y\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $y\ge0$ and $\sum_{i\in K}y_i\le1$ for every chain $K$ of $P$. With $h(z)=-\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]}\ln z_i$, the entropy of $P$ is $H(P)=\min_{z\in C(P)}h(z)$, a special case of graph entropy for the comparability graph. Its averaged variant is $QH(P)=\mathbb{E}_{z\in C(P)}[h(z)]$, the expectation for $z$ uniform in $C(P)$, which lies in $[1,H_n]$. Here $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. Kahn and Kim showed that $\mathrm{LB}(P)=n(\ln n-H(P))$ approximates $\ln|\Delta(P)|$ within a constant factor (in fact $\ln|\Delta(P)|\le\mathrm{LB}(P)\le2\ln|\Delta(P)|$). The authors show that the quantum adversary lower bound for this sorting problem is, up to a constant, $\mathrm{QLB}(P)=n(H_n-QH(P))$. By analysing this bound they prove Yao's conjecture, that quantum query complexity is $\Omega(\log|\Delta(P)|)$, for series-parallel posets and an extended class. Their findings support the conjecture that $\mathrm{LB}$ and $\mathrm{QLB}$ are always within a constant factor, which would give Yao's conjecture for all posets. Proving it requires understanding how $H(P)$ and $QH(P)$ compare, but tools are lacking: unlike the entropy, $\mathbb{E}_{z\in C}[h(z)]$ is not monotone under inclusion of the convex corner $C$. This is order theory / quantum complexity rather than graph theory.
